item.description: Using astrochronology, Wang et al. estimate that relative sea-level change led benthic turnover by ~70,000 years during the late Cambrian SPICE event under their age model, supporting links among orbital forcing, marine anoxia and biodiversity loss. The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations. item.description: Abstract Sediment respiration in streams/rivers impacts global biogeochemical cycles, yet is mostly studied under perennially-inundated conditions despite all river corridors having variably inundated areas and most streams going dry each year. Previous experiments observed sediment rewetting to cause elevated or suppressed aerobic respiration, indicating variation across studies. To deepen understanding, we conducted 21-day wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams spread across the contiguous United States. Here we show that drying and rewetting sediments from perennial and non-perennial streams had near-neutral effects or suppressed O 2 consumption rates. These biogeochemical cold moments contrast previous studies that observed hot moments. Sediment texture and microbial activity explained variation in responses to rewetting, but this did not reveal why some studies observed cold moments while others observed hot moments. To solve this we propose a unifying conceptual model whereby hot and cold moments exist simultaneously upon rewetting by considering both dry-state and perennially-inundated reference points. item.title: Local growth laws determine global shape of molluscan shells
item.dc:creator: Huan Liu
Kaushik Bhattacharya
item.prism:publicationName: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
item.description: Molluscan shells come in various shapes and sizes. Despite this diversity, each species produces a shell with a characteristic shape that is independent of environmental conditions. We seek to understand this robust complexity. We are guided by two principles in the spirit of D’Arcy Thompson. First, the growth is governed by the repeated and continuous application of a fixed growth law, even as the shell evolves in overall shape, without any complex biological machinery to monitor and control the growth. Second, the growth law depends solely on local geometry at the shell’s growing edge. The first principle naturally leads to the mathematical statement that the shape of the shell is generated by the action of a Lie group on a protoconch. The second naturally leads to a particular representation of the Lie group. We use this representation to show that the shapes of nearly all known molluscan shells can be described by essentially three parameters: a scalar (scaling), a vector (orientation), and a curve (edge of the protoconch). We relate these parameters to the phylogenetic tree. In addition to the morphogenetic insight, our results potentially point to a alternative growth-based approach to engineering complex structures. item.description: Abstract Enhanced weathering, adding crushed silicate minerals to soils, is being explored as a way to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide, but its effects on soil organic carbon remain uncertain. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. In a 55-week soil microcosm experiment, adding olivine alone reduces total soil organic carbon. Adding olivine with glucose initially suppresses microbial carbon uptake, but by week 55 instead boosts microbial biomass and mineral-associated organic matter more than glucose alone, while lowering respiratory carbon loss. These late-stage gains grow stronger alongside geochemical signs of mineral weathering. Nanoscale imaging shows that newly formed soil organic carbon accumulates within pre-existing organic and mineral microsites rather than directly on olivine or newly formed clay surfaces. Our findings suggest that when labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage primarily through microbial processing, rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon to bind to. item.description: Abstract Nutrient enrichment and warming cause widespread costal deoxygenation, leading to hypoxia or even anoxia in bottom waters. The benthic-water-column-feedbacks that develop under persistent seasonal oxygen depletion and amplify hypoxia remain poorly constrained. A 15-month study of a seasonally hypoxic to anoxic costal system in the southwestern Baltic Sea combined water-column monitoring, sediment chemistry, metabolic rates and microbial analyses with historic data to reveal pronounced seasonal shifts in sediment processes. During winter oxygenation, organic matter degradation, fermentation, aerobic respiration, nitrate- and iron-reduction and microbial competition increased. Re-ventilation following anoxia did not reset sediment biogeochemistry, but initiated intensified oxygen consumption, microbial biosynthetic activity and anaerobic carbon re-cycling. Reactive ironoxyhydroxides became exhausted, the sulfidic zone shoaled and sulfate reduction and pyrite formation rates increased through fall. These processes reinforced benthic feedbacks, progressively reducing the sediment’s capacity to retain sulfide over years. This weakening of sedimentary resilience exacerbates sulfide accumulation in eutrophic costal environments with growing chances of sulfidic deep-water upwelling. item.description: Abstract Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized. item.title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport
item.dc:creator: Soumendu Sarkar
Rondi M. Davies
Qiwei Zhang
Luísa D. V. Carvalho

item.description: This study links higher diamond grades in kimberlites to water-rich olivine. Modeling suggests that rapid magma ascent preserves higher olivine water contents and facilitates efficient diamond transport, highlighting ascent rate as a key control on diamond preservation. Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency. item.description: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere. item.description: Metamorphic proteins challenge the single-sequence-structure-function paradigm by switching between distinct folds that often adopt complementary functions. However, the conformational states sampled along the fold-switching pathway have remained elusive because they are transient and unstable. Using multinuclear chemical exchange saturation transfer and relaxation dispersion NMR, combined with chemical shift–based structure determination and protein engineering, we visualized the atomic resolution structure of an “invisible” state of the metamorphic chemokine lymphotactin. This state is a chimera that integrates the secondary and tertiary structure of one fold with the quaternary assembly of the other. Locking lymphotactin into a single conformation abolishes access to this state, supporting its role as an on-pathway intermediate in metamorphosis. The stabilization of such hybrid intermediates is likely to have facilitated the evolution of fold-switching and represents a powerful strategy for protein design. item.description: Mass-independent isotope fractionation (MIF) of oxygen provides key insights into atmospheric chemistry and the origin of isotopic anomalies in planetary materials. To date, MIF has been primarily associated with gas-phase processes involving symmetry-dependent reaction pathways, most notably ozone formation. Whether analogous effects can arise in condensed phases or at interfaces remains an open question. Here we report laboratory experiments demonstrating that energetic particle irradiation of icy oxide surfaces produces mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation at temperatures as low as 10 K. Electron irradiation of SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 substrates in the presence of H 2 O ice results in measurable shifts in Δ 17 O in the underlying solids. The resulting three-isotope relationships include slope-1-like behavior in SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 and distinct, substrate-dependent trends in Al 2 O 3 , indicating that irradiation-induced defect formation and interfacial chemistry govern the isotope effects. The magnitude of the observed anomalies demonstrates that irradiation-driven processes can generate substantial oxygen isotope heterogeneity in condensed phases. These results identify a previously unrecognized class of MIF and provide a quantitative framework for interpreting oxygen isotope signatures in radiation-processed environments, including interstellar grains and early solar system materials. item.title: Effusive sedimentary volcanism experimentally reproduced under Martian-like conditions
item.dc:creator: Ondřej Krýza

item.description: Abstract Rapid boiling, cooling, and freezing are commonly assumed to rapidly quench metastable liquid eruptions exposed to near-vacuum planetary environments, influencing both sedimentary volcanism on Mars and cryovolcanism on icy worlds. However, how these coupled phase transitions govern eruptive processes remains largely unknown. Here we show experimentally that boiling instead sustains coupled ballistic-effusive mud eruptions under Martian-like pressure conditions (~4.5 mbar). Using an ice-sealed metastable reservoir, we reproduced subsurface-driven eruptions initiated by internally generated boiling-induced overpressure. Eruptions evolved systematically from short-lived ballistic fountains toward episodic effusive emplacement accompanied by coherent mud-flow formation. Ballistic transport redistributed liquid mud around the vent and promoted proximal accumulation that subsequently coalesced into sustained flows despite ongoing cooling and freezing. Numerical modeling further demonstrates that erupted mud would remain largely unfrozen during ballistic transport under Martian gravity conditions. Together, our results show that rapid boiling does not suppress sedimentary volcanism under low-pressure conditions, but instead actively sustains eruptive transport and surface emplacement. These findings provide new constraints on this process on Mars and establish a broader physical framework for metastable liquid eruptions across the Solar System. item.description: The destruction of the North China Craton (NCC) during the Mesozoic was accompanied by widespread felsic magmatism, intense deformation, and world-class gold mineralization, yet the temporal and genetic coupling between subduction-driven crustal thickening, lithospheric thinning, and giant gold mineralization remains poorly resolved. To address this gap, we integrate field observations, petrography, zircon U–Pb geochronology, Lu–Hf isotopes, and whole-rock geochemistry for granitoid intrusions from the Jiaodong Peninsula on the southeastern NCC margin. Three magmatic episodes are identified at ca. 160 Ma, 130 Ma, and 120 Ma. The ca. 160 Ma adakitic granitoids originated from partial melting of thickened lower continental crust. The ca. 130 Ma granitoids were generated from ancient continental crust with minimal mantle input, whereas the ca. 120 Ma granitoids record prominent crust–mantle mixing involving recycled continental crust and enriched lithospheric mantle. The new chronological, geochemical, and isotopic data show two abrupt shifts at ca. 130 Ma and 120 Ma, together indicating progressive increases in mantle-derived heat and material contributions. These lines of evidence delineate a tectonic transition from compression to extension at ca. 130 Ma, driven by the Paleo-Pacific Plate’s shift from flat to steep subduction, followed by peak lithospheric delamination at ca. 120 Ma, which triggered intensive crust–mantle interaction magmatism that was temporally coincident with giant gold deposition. Collectively, our results establish a refined temporal framework for Mesozoic geodynamic switching in the southeastern NCC and demonstrate that lithospheric modification via changes in subduction angle is a primary controlling factor for the genesis of giant gold deposits, advancing the understanding of how deep geodynamic processes regulate continental gold metallogenesis. item.title: Recycling of juvenile arc crust in an ancient convergent margin revealed by Hg isotopes
item.dc:creator: Han Qi
Jun-Hong Zhao
Runsheng Yin

item.description: Recycling of newly formed arc crust at convergent margins is critical to the long-term balance between growth and destruction of the continental crust. However, identifying this process in ancient convergent systems remains challenging because direct geological evidence is rarely preserved. Here, we measure Hg stable isotopes and Nd–Hf radiogenic isotopes in subduction-related igneous rocks from the Neoproterozoic (870–730 Ma) active continental margin of the Yangtze Block in South China to investigate the recycling of juvenile arc crust. Both mafic rocks and granitoids exhibit variable whole-rock Δ199Hg values that largely overlap the depleted-mantle range, ranging from −0.13‰ to +0.15‰ (mean = −0.04 ± 0.15‰, 2SD) and −0.18‰ to +0.11‰ (mean = −0.05 ± 0.14‰, 2SD), respectively, suggesting variable contributions from mantle-, marine-, and terrestrial-derived Hg. Samples with negative Δ199Hg signatures show variable but mostly positive whole-rock εNd (−3.4 to +6.4) and positive zircon εHf (+1.8 to +14.7), and all samples with Δ199Hg below the depleted mantle range (< −0.10‰) have positive εNd values (+0.3 to +3.1). These combined isotopic characteristics indicate that terrigenous sediments formed by weathering and erosion of juvenile arc crust and carrying terrestrial-derived Hg were recycled into the mantle source of arc magmas. Such recycling was likely achieved through subduction of arc-derived trench sediments and/or tectonic erosion of forearc materials. The results of this work suggest that recycling of newly formed arc crust in convergent margins may have been an overlooked means of crustal destruction throughout Earth’s history. item.title: Calcium isotope systematics during multistage seafloor alteration of abyssal peridotites: insights from the Gakkel Ridge
item.dc:creator: Jia-Wei Xiong
Chuan-Zhou Liu
Yin-Zheng Lin
Yang Xu
item.description: Calcium is readily mobilized and redistributed during seafloor alteration of abyssal peridotites, yet the associated isotope effects of serpentinization and carbonation are difficult to distinguish from inherited magmatic signatures. Here we combine thermodynamic modelling and whole-rock geochemistry with selective leaching experiments to disentangle these contributions in a petrographically classified suite of Gakkel Ridge peridotites. Thermodynamic melting calculations coupled with internally consistent mineral–melt fractionation factors provide a reference frame for both Ca contents and isotope compositions. Relatively fresh peridotites have δ 44/40Ca values of 0.88–0.94‰, slightly below the predicted residual values, consistent with minor carbonate addition and/or prior melt–rock interaction. In contrast, serpentinized peridotites lacking visible carbonate generally record substantial Ca loss and span a wide δ 44/40Ca range of 0.59–1.19‰. Calculations of selective orthopyroxene and clinopyroxene consumption yield distinct isotope trajectories depending on the evolving Ca contributions of the two pyroxenes and the adopted mineral–fluid fractionation factors. None of the results reproduces the lowest measured values, which likely reflect inherited magmatic signatures and/or unmodelled kinetic effects. In carbonated samples, carbonate-rich leachates account for ∼ 59–100% of whole-rock Ca, with δ 44/40Ca values down to − 0.11‰ in aragonite-dominated fractions and up to 1.43‰ in calcite-dominated fractions. Carbonate addition can thus dominate the whole-rock isotope budget, with the direction of the shift set by the dominant polymorph. These results collectively show that altered oceanic mantle is highly heterogeneous in Ca isotope composition, and that carbonated oceanic mantle spans both light and heavy signatures. This pre-subduction heterogeneity should be considered when interpreting Ca isotope evidence for recycled carbonate in the deep Earth. item.title: Continental OIB magmatism reveals asthenospheric heterogeneity driven by deep carbon recycling in postcollisional southeastern Tibet
item.dc:creator: Jing Chen
Dapeng Li
Jifeng Xu
Jian Sun
Jiarun Tu
Benyan Xu

item.description: The formation of the Tibetan Plateau and the subsequent postcollisional convergence have left profound imprints on the lithosphere, yet how these processes have modified the underlying upper mantle remains poorly constrained due to the lack of direct magmatic records. Continental ocean-island-type basalts, although volumetrically minor, provide an exceptional window into such compositional overprinting by deep geodynamic processes. Here, we probe heterogeneity in the postcollisional asthenosphere by integrating mineralogical, elemental, and Mg-Zn-Sr-Nd isotopic constraints from continental basalts in the Tongguan region, southeastern Tibetan Plateau. These basalts erupted during the Quaternary (ca. 1 Ma; zircon U-Pb ages) and exhibit typical ocean-island basalt (OIB)–type trace element signatures with depleted Sr-Nd isotopic compositions (εNd ≤ +8.6). Mineral and whole-rock thermometry, hygrometry, and oxybarometry collectively indicate a relatively hydrous (H2O ≤ 3.5 wt%) yet low-fO2 (FMQ+0.1) primary magma that formed under normal mantle thermal conditions (<1368 °C). Olivine chemistry and whole-rock elemental systematics consistently require derivation from a dominantly Stage 2 pyroxenitic asthenospheric mantle with minor peridotite involvement. The basalts display systematically light δ26Mg (−0.60‰ to −0.49‰) and heavy δ66Zn (+0.34‰ to +0.42‰) values yet lack elemental signatures of carbonate metasomatism. This marked isotope–element decoupling compellingly traces recycled marine carbonates that underwent deep subduction-induced decarbonation, leaving a “ghost carbonate” imprint in the mantle source. Together with geophysical evidence, these features directly link Tongguan basaltic magmatism to dehydration of stagnant oceanic slabs in the mantle transition zone (MTZ). The Mg-Zn isotopic variations further delineate a clear regional imprint of recycled sedimentary carbonates in the asthenospheric mantle south of ~26°N as a consequence of deep slab stagnation, in stark contrast to the relatively noncarbonated asthenosphere to the north, where slab tearing dominates. Taken together, our study demonstrates that continental OIB-type magmatism in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau records pronounced postcollisional asthenospheric heterogeneity dictated by spatially variable subduction dynamics. More broadly, this case highlights the pivotal role of stagnant slabs in the MTZ in governing deep carbon recycling and generating asthenosphere-derived continental OIB-type magmatism. item.title: Multi-Stage Carbonatite Magmatism Drives Rare Earth Element Enrichment
item.dc:creator: Lucas Tatnell
Andrea Giuliani
Isra Ezad
Christopher M Fisher

Stephen Centrella

Marco Fiorentini
item.description: Rare earth elements (REE) are crucial for the green-energy transition, with the largest REE deposits occurring in carbonatites. Either magmatic differentiation or hydrothermal remobilization are considered primary mineralizing mechanisms for ore-grade REE enrichment. Here, we test and quantify the hypothesis that during protracted carbonatite magmatism, late carbonatitic brines/brine-melts from younger magmatic events strip REE from previously crystallized primary calcite (± apatite ± REE phases), progressively concentrating REE in the fluid phase. We demonstrate quantitatively that primary calcite in the Twihinate carbonatite complex, Morocco, loses > 50% of its ∼ 0.1 wt% REE during reaction with late carbonatitic brines/brine-melts. Textures and carbonate chemistry show that removal of REE from calcite by these fluids occurs throughout the complex. Mass balance implies that enough calcite is available to source all required metal for ore formation. Comparable observations across carbonatites worldwide indicate that remobilization of REE from primary calcite (± apatite ± REE phases) by residual magmatic fluids may represent a fundamental mechanism for REE mineralization in carbonatite systems. item.title: Lithospheric structural and magmatic fractionation controls on the giant Ag metallogenic belt in the Great Xing'an Range
item.dc:creator: Kaixuan Hui
Kezhang Qin
Bertrand Rottier
Mingjian Cao

item.description: Magmatic-hydrothermal silver deposits are the main source of silver and commonly distributed along metallogenic belts. However, the processes responsible for the massive silver endowment of silver metallogenic belts remain poorly understood. This review integrates whole-rock geochemistry with NdHf isotope mapping in the Great Xing'an Range metallogenic belt (GXMB), China, to reveal the link between silver mineralization, lithospheric architecture, and magmatic evolution. Whole-rock Nd and zircon Hf isotope mapping of the Mesozoic intermediate-felsic rocks in the GXMB reveals that 70% of the belt consists of juvenile isotopic domains with εNd(t) > 0 and εHf(t) > +4.5. The large silver deposits preferentially occur in the most juvenile isotopic domains with εNd(t) > +1.5 and εHf(t) > +6.5, particularly along the paleo-sutures or intersections of the paleo-sutures and major faults. However, εNd(t) and εHf(t) values of the Ag-related felsic igneous rocks exhibit significant heterogeneity among deposits, suggesting that the proportion of juvenile material involved in magmatic evolution is not the primary or sole determinant of magma fertility. The deposits with the largest Ag reserves are associated with highly evolved AgSn mineralization systems and contain cassiterite and canfieldite. In addition, the Ag-related felsic igneous rocks are characterized by a high degree of magmatic fractionation. These suggest that high magmatic differentiation played an important role in Ag enrichment in the GXMB. We propose that paleo-sutures and structural junctions are major conduits for juvenile magmas, allowing their accumulation and differentiation into large magmatic reservoirs. A high degree of magmatic fractionation enriches Ag in the residual melt and promotes its efficient extraction into exsolved fluids. Finally, fluid exsolution from the highly fractionated melt from those reservoirs will lead to the formation of silver deposits in the GXMB. item.description: The genesis of Au deposits in low-grade metamorphic rocks has long been controversial. item.description: The presence of ocean-island basalt (OIB)-type magmas in convergent margins implies complex mantle geodynamic processes. This study reports an Early Permian (ca. 282 Ma) association of OIB-type and Nb-enriched arc-type rocks from the Northern Qiangtang Terrane, Tibet. Both suites share predominantly depleted Nd-Hf isotopic compositions, suggesting derivation from an asthenospheric mantle containing enriched components. The Nb-enriched arc-type rocks additionally record slab interaction. Spatial distribution with OIB-type rocks located proximal and arc-type rocks distal to the trench supports a sub-slab origin for the enriched component. After a systematic evaluation of various potential geodynamic models, we interpret this origin as reflecting slab tearing in the vicinity of the trench. Spatiotemporal, geochemical, and thermal comparisons suggest that this mantle source may be linked to the 290–285 Ma Qiangtang-Panjal large igneous province, which was located >2000 km to the south. This linkage implies long-distance transport of plume material across the Paleo-Tethys Ocean and subsequent plume-subduction zone interaction beneath the Northern Qiangtang margin. We propose that slab tearing facilitated the upwelling and melting of this previously enriched material, providing the setting for long-distance plume material transport and plume-subduction interaction in ancient convergent systems. The transport of plume material was likely driven by large-scale northward mantle flow. This large-scale mantle-flow framework may also provide a qualitative working hypothesis for linking plume-related thermal weakening and basal traction to the initial rifting and northward drift of the Cimmerian microcontinents. item.description: Well-preserved epithermal Cu-Zn-Au mineralization is rare in the Precambrian. The adjacent Bamhani area displays classic IS textures such as colloform banding and comb quartz, together with significant Zn-Pb enrichment, likely precipitated from low-temperature (as low as 125 °C) and moderately saline fluids resulting from mixing of magmatic and meteoric waters. Sulfur isotope values from both regions (δ34S: −2.57‰ to +4.14‰ Vienna Canyon Diablo Troilite) are consistent with a dominant magmatic sulfur source, with minor crustal input observed in the distal regions. item.description: Devonian magmatism in the Eastern Sierras Pampeanas of Argentina is characterized by voluminous monzogranitic to granitic intrusions and associated mafic to intermediate rocks with sanukitoid affinity. Trace-element systematics (e.g., Ba, Sr, Zr, REEs, F) and Sr-Nd isotopic compositions suggest that the primary magmas were derived from a lithospheric mantle source metasomatized by crust-derived components during earlier orogenic stages. The widespread occurrence and substantial volume of these granitoids, estimated at over 6,000 km3, highlight their potential contribution to net continental crust growth. This study provides the first robust evidence of Phanerozoic post-collisional mantle-derived magmatism in South America. The Devonian batholiths of the Sierras Pampeanas thus represent a key example of juvenile crust generation far from active continental margins, involving partial melting of a lithospheric mantle source previously enriched during earlier orogenic stages. Melt generation and accumulation may have contributed to lithospheric weakening during regional post-orogenic extension. item.description: Two working hypotheses explain the tectonic evolution of the collage of geologic elements comprising the Northern Cordillera of Alaska and Yukon: a long-term eastward subduction scenario and a westward-then-eastward subduction scenario. The consilience of geological evidence and geophysical evidence in the form of seismic tomography corroborates the westward-then-eastward subduction scenario. item.description: Carbonate minerals are fundamental components of the sedimentary record, yet their mineralogical and textural diversity cannot be understood from equilibrium thermodynamics or any single crystallization model alone. This review develops an evidence-constrained, pathway-dependent framework that links carbonate nucleation, growth and transformation processes with environmental modulation, structural inheritance, and their expression in the sedimentary record. We distinguish prenucleation solution states from condensed-phase formation and subsequent growth, treating stable prenucleation clusters as a debated model, while integrating ion-by-ion growth, liquid–liquid phase separation, amorphous precursors, particle-mediated growth, and oriented attachment within a common pathway framework. Environmental variables-including supersaturation, temperature, ionic composition, organic matter, EPS, and microbial activity-jointly bias the accessibility, persistence, and transformation of these pathways. Crystallization histories may generate nanoscale structural and compositional features that are selectively inherited by larger-scale carbonate textures; however, pathway–mineral–texture relationships are non-unique, and robust interpretation requires convergent mineralogical, crystallographic, microstructural, geochemical, temporal, and environmental evidence. Applied to the dolomite problem, this framework emphasizes multiple, system-dependent routes by which kinetic barriers to Mg incorporation and Ca–Mg ordering may be overcome, rather than a universal precursor sequence. Together, these elements define an evidence-constrained, non-deterministic pathway–mineral–texture framework that integrates molecular- to nanoscale crystallization processes with environmental modulation, selective structural inheritance, and diagenetic modification, allowing crystallization histories to be evaluated through convergent evidence rather than inferred from mineral identity or texture alone. item.description: The paleogeographic position of the South China Craton (SCC) within Rodinia remains debated between two competing models: peripheral versus interior within the supercontinent. item.description: Field, petrographic, and isotopic data indicate that the compositionally zoned lithium-caesium‑tantalum (LCT) pegmatites in the thermal aureole of the Adamello batholith (Italian Alps) formed by low degrees of anatexis of metasedimentary rocks. item.description: This study presents the first Moroccan Cu and Fe isotopic data (δ65Cu and δ56Fe) on (hypogene and) supergene minerals from three polymetallic deposits (Tazalaght, Agoujgal, and Bou Skour) located in the Anti-Atlas Copperbelt. These findings underscore the importance of detailed mineralogical and geochemical characterization to interpret both Cu and Fe isotopic data, in order to reconstruct ore-forming supergene processes and fluid evolution in weathering profiles. item.description: The Triassic platform carbonates of the Eastern and Southern Alps host over 500 Pb-Zn deposits collectively known as Alpine-type (AT) Pb-Zn deposits. item.description: Abstract Subseafloor hydrothermal circulation drives biogeochemical exchange between the solid Earth and its ocean, and could play a similar role in other ocean worlds. This well‐studied, moderate T system (∼65°C–70°C in the upper ocean crust) represents a warm end‐member on Earth, with slow flow across 10s of kilometers. Modest lateral flow between recharge and discharge sites is accompanied by small‐scale convection, resulting in variable local T and flow conditions, even for simple, layered models. The flow and T fields are time‐varying, with the magnitudes of subseafloor variation oscillating around quasi‐steady conditions. The fractions of the crustal aquifer that are in T ranges relevant to different microbial habitats were calculated. In simulations with discharging fluids at ∼70°C, temperatures of 40°C–80°C were found within 65%–90% of the aquifer. The same simulation, run with low gravity appropriate for Europa, has 50%–70% of the aquifer at temperatures of 40°C–80°C, and 30%–50% at T > 80°C. Geochemical modeling based on these simulations indicates that some nutrients and organic molecules in the fluids for this end‐member case could vary in concentration up to an order of magnitude as a consequence of such T variability. item.description: Extreme hydroclimatic changes linked to greenhouse gas emissions from large igneous provinces are exemplified by the Carnian Pluvial Episode (CPE; ca. 233 Ma), during which volcanic activity drove shifts in the hydrological cycle, though marine records offer only indirect evidence of terrestrial changes. Still, the reliability of the data is difficult to evaluate, due to the absence of detailed sampling and information on mechanisms. Here we present a multiproxy analysis (including organic carbon isotopes, mercury [Hg] concentrations and isotopes, trace elements, and zircon U-Pb dating) in the Ordos Basin, North China. We can identify the onset of volcanic activity in this record based on Hg enrichment and near-zero mass-independent fractionation of Hg isotopes, which serve as proxies for volcanism, and find that these three onsets are broadly coeval with enhanced terrestrial runoff and rapid lake expansion. The most obvious episode of Hg enrichment and negative carbon isotope excursions during interval I is consistent with massive releases of local volcanogenic Hg and carbon to the Earth-surface system. Within the CPE interval, carbon isotope and sedimentary records indicate that the latter two pulses of depleted carbon into the atmosphere–lacustrine system were linked to discrete enhancements of the hydrological cycle. Our results provide a direct link between volcanism and its impact on the hydrological and carbon cycles.
